note: Codes must stay in the form I<n> / E<n>. Labels are kept short (under ~36 characters) so they fit the PRISMA diagram box; the full wording is in 'description'. Both screeners must use the same file.

include.label: Peer-reviewed full paper, English
include.description: Peer-reviewed full paper articles, including journal papers, conference papers, books, and book chapters, published in English.

include.label: Published 2018 – Sept 2026
include.description: Research published between 2018 and September 2026, to ensure relevance to recent developments in generative AI and XR technology.

include.label: Learned generative model in VR/AR/MR
include.description: Research applying learned generative models, such as LLMs, GANs, and diffusion models, in VR, AR, or MR systems.

include.label: Presents/applies generative XR
include.description: Articles that present or apply a generative XR system or technique.

include.label: Evaluates the generative XR system
include.description: Studies that evaluate a generative XR system through user studies, technical metrics, benchmark comparisons, or expert evaluation.

include.label: GenAI for content, interaction or UX
include.description: The generative model generates XR content (e.g., assets, scenes, audio, motion), supports interaction (selection, manipulation, navigation, system control, or symbolic input), or shapes the user experience (e.g., personalization).

exclude.label: Non-English, short paper or abstract
exclude.description: Studies published in languages other than English, or short papers, posters, and extended abstracts.

exclude.label: Published before 2018
exclude.description: Studies published before 2018, to focus on the period when learned generative models became practical for XR.

exclude.label: No learned model, or not essential
exclude.description: Studies that do not use a learned generative model, where the model is not essential to the system, or where it is not used in an XR system.

exclude.label: Conceptual, opinion or review
exclude.description: Conceptual papers, opinion pieces, surveys, and reviews.

exclude.label: No evaluation reported
exclude.description: Papers that do not report any evaluation of the system.

exclude.label: GenAI not for content/interaction/UX
exclude.description: The generative model's role falls outside content generation, interaction, or user experience.

research_questions.text: What generative AI content-creation techniques are applied in XR?
research_questions.look_for: Method: what the model makes (3D assets, scenes, textures, audio, motion, dialogue) and how (text-to-3D, diffusion, LLM layout…).

research_questions.text: How are these content-creation techniques distributed across output types, model architectures, computational infrastructure, generation timing, and application domains?
research_questions.look_for: Method + system overview figure: output type, named model, cloud vs on-device, runtime vs offline generation, application domain.

research_questions.text: What interaction techniques in XR involve generative AI?
research_questions.look_for: Interaction / system section: how the user triggers or steers generation (voice, natural language, gesture, sketch, gaze, agent).

research_questions.text: How do these interaction paradigms compare to those in non-generative XR systems?
research_questions.look_for: Study design: a baseline condition with conventional (non-generative) interaction.

research_questions.text: What computational costs and benefits are reported for generative XR systems?
research_questions.look_for: Results / implementation: latency, generation time, FPS, GPU / memory, API cost, quality metrics.

research_questions.text: How do these costs and benefits compare to prior non-generative approaches, such as procedural generation?
research_questions.look_for: Results: a comparison against procedural, manual or other non-generative pipelines.

research_questions.text: How does generative AI affect user experience in XR compared to non-generative systems?
research_questions.look_for: User study: UX measures (presence, SUS, NASA-TLX, engagement, interviews), ideally against a non-generative condition.

fulltext_skim.note: One check at a time, cheapest and most decisive first. The first check a paper fails is its exclusion reason. About 2 minutes per paper. The RQ hints say what to notice while you are in that part of the paper; they are not extra criteria.

steps.title: Format and language
steps.where: First page, page count, venue track
steps.look: English? A full paper, not a poster, demo, work-in-progress, extended abstract or short paper (about 4 pages or fewer, or an Adjunct / Abstracts / Posters track).

steps.title: Evaluation
steps.where: Section headings, results tables and figures
steps.look: Is there a user study, technical metrics, benchmark comparison or expert evaluation? A demo, use case or 'future work' alone fails.

steps.title: Kind of paper
steps.where: End of abstract, contribution list in the introduction
steps.look: Does it present or apply a system or technique? Surveys, reviews, position or vision papers and conceptual frameworks fail.

steps.title: Learned generative model
steps.look: Names a learned generative model (LLM, diffusion, GAN, VAE, text-to-3D, TTS…). Essential: remove it and the system no longer does its main job. Used in a VR/AR/MR system. Procedural or rule-based generation, or only discriminative ML (detection, classification, pose), fails.

steps.title: Role of the model
steps.where: Same method pass: what the model outputs
steps.look: Its output is XR content, supports interaction (selection, manipulation, navigation, system control, symbolic input) or shapes the user experience. Training-data augmentation or offline analytics only fails.

research_questions_note: Shown as hints under the full-text checks listed in fulltext_skim.steps[].rqs.
